correctness.rationale: The hyperelliptic degree-two map has 6 points on P1(F5), so at most 12 rational points, with equality precisely if all six fibers split and are unramified. Lagrange interpolation produces exactly 2^5*2*5=320 binary sextics with F5 values {1,4} at all six base points. Independently enumerated all 320, computed polynomial gcd with derivative, found exactly 240 smooth sextics; independent factor degrees give 120 (2,4), 40 (3,3), 80 (6). Independently applied all 120 PGL2(F5) transformations and both square scalar factors, getting exactly three orbits of sizes 120,40,80; separate F25 quadratic-field exact enumeration gives counts 26/28/24 and by Newton identities Weil middle coefficients 18/19/17. PGL2 equivalence of genus-two hyperelliptic models is justified by uniqueness of hyperelliptic involution. Complete finite enumeration is a proof here, not a heuristic sample.

originality.rationale: General 12-point bound, existence and PGL2-orbit method are known. Nart 2007 computes unrestricted totals of hyperelliptic classes but not the six-split-fiber sublocus and its branch/zeta joint table in the inspected theorem. Hernández Encinas–Menezes–Muñoz Masqué (2002) explicitly assumes characteristic different from 2 and 5 and a rational Weierstrass point, whereas these F5 extremal curves have no rational branch point; so that seeming exact classification is inapplicable. No demonstrated stronger database coverage of the exact three-way refinement, but all-genus-two finite-field catalogues remain a live priority risk.
residual_risks: An uninspected specialist catalogue of genus-two curves over F5 might already encode exactly these 12-point classes, factor partitions and zeta polynomials.
